claim: Diffusion is the cheapest way to make twenty separately generated shots feel like one film, which is why it should be set high in the hierarchy and inherited. Pro_mist lifts the blacks and haloes every floodlight; heavy_diffusion turns the whole frame into a memory.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: clean lens, crisp contrast, no diffusion
light diffusion filter, gentle halo on highlights
pro-mist filter, misty halation, lifted blacks
heavy diffusion, dreamy soft focus, blooming highlights
smoked glass filter, hazy, muted contrast

review.issue: none is baseline plus a negation, and light_diffusion ("light diffusion filter, gentle halo on highlights") is a weaker phrasing of pro_mist ("pro-mist filter, misty halation, lifted blacks"); smoke_glass ("hazy, muted contrast") sits on the same haze axis. Six options, probably three separable looks.
review.fix: none → empty clause; merge light_diffusion into pro_mist; keep heavy_diffusion as the extreme and glimmer as the genuine outlier ("sparkle" is a strong trained anime tag, so that panel really will diverge); keep smoke_glass only if it drops "hazy" and leans on "muted contrast, desaturated".
